cartridges.name: .308 Winchester

diameterSource.text: Bullet diameter 0.308 in, as listed on the bullet makers' pages.

cartridges.velocityLossNote: Rifleshooter.com cut one .308 barrel from 28 to 16.5 inches and measured Federal Gold Medal 168 gr at each length: 20.9 fps lost per inch on average. It is one barrel and one test, not manufacturer data. Your rifle will differ, so chronograph your load.

cartridges.name: .223 Remington

diameterSource.text: SAAMI .223 Remington drawing: bullet diameter .2245 - .0030 in.

cartridges.velocityLossNote: No barrel-length correction is made for this cartridge. The published figures disagree: PMC's own two-barrel velocities work out to 37 to 45 fps per inch, and one independent cut-down test measured 22 to 30. The app shows the maker's velocity with its test barrel. Chronograph your load.

safetyNote.text: However, it is not safe to shoot “5.56,” “5.56 NATO,” or “5.56x45mm” ammunition in a barrel marked as being chambered in 223 Remington for a number of reasons. The main reason being that a barrel marked as chambered in 223 Remington will have a shorter throat into the rifling than a “5.56” barrel which may cause increased pressure if the “5.56” ammunition is fired in it. This can result in serious injury or death to the user and/or bystanders, as well as damage to the firearm.

loads.name: Federal Gold Medal 168 gr Sierra MatchKing (GM308M)
loads.note: Federal does not state its test barrel length, so the app cannot correct this velocity for your barrel. The difference is about 2%.
